title: Build Verification Lab — System Overview
description: The lab takes a project directory, runs it through syntax → run → tests, and records an honest verdict.

title: Stage 1 — Syntax: node --check on Every File
t: Stage 1 — Syntax: node --check on Every File
description: Every .js file in the project must parse; failures are reported per file with the real error text.

title: Stage 2 — Run: Execute the Entry File
t: Stage 2 — Run: Execute the Entry File
description: The entry file runs under node with captured stdout, stderr, exit code, and timeout protection.

title: Stage 3 — Tests: Declared Expectations Checked
description: Each test runs a command and passes only on exit 0 plus the expected output substring.

title: Failure Is Recorded, Not Hidden
description: A broken program produces a recorded failure with the real error — the lab never pretends it passed.

title: Fix and Re-Run — The Redemption Loop
t: Fix and Re-Run — The Redemption Loop
description: A fixed project re-verified: fail → fix → pass, with both reports on record.

title: Report Format — What a Verdict Contains
t: Report Format — What a Verdict Contains
description: Every verdict carries per-stage results, pass counts, and the earned verification status.

title: Multi-File Projects — Every File Gets Checked
t: Multi-File Projects — Every File Gets Checked
description: Syntax runs over all .js files in the directory, not just the entry point.

title: Timeout Protection — Infinite Loops Are Killed, Not Waited On
t: Timeout Protection — Infinite Loops Are Killed, Not Waited On
description: Any stage exceeding 8 seconds is terminated and recorded as timed out.

title: Interfaces — verifyProject and the Three Stages
t: Interfaces — verifyProject and the Three Stages
description: verifyProject(dir, opts) is the whole lab; stageSyntax, stageRun, stageTests are exported separately.

title: Usage Guide — Verify a Directory in One Call
t: Usage Guide — Verify a Directory in One Call
description: verifyProject(dir, {entry, tests, args}) returns the full verdict; the CLI mirrors it.

title: Limits and Honest Boundaries
description: The lab verifies Node.js programs locally; it cannot test browser behavior, networks, or other languages.

title: Integration — The Lab Verifies Generator Output
t: Integration — The Lab Verifies Generator Output
description: The master's generator→lab handoff, executed for real: build a spec, verify the project, print the verdict.

title: Self-Check — All Five System Files Pass node --check
t: Self-Check — All Five System Files Pass node --check
description: The lab turns its syntax stage on its own family: all five system modules parse cleanly.

title: Audit Trail — Every Verdict Is Reproducible Evidence
t: Audit Trail — Every Verdict Is Reproducible Evidence
description: Verdicts carry stage details and captured output, so any result can be re-examined later.
